title: An Iranian Vision of the New Middle East
gist: Iran's former foreign minister writes that the U.S. has resumed attacks on Iran after the Switzerland memorandum of understanding collapsed, and attributes the collapse to divergent U.S. and Iranian readings of the deal's Strait of Hormuz provisions — with Tehran believing it had only committed to 'best efforts' arrangements. The captured text is a paywalled teaser that cuts off mid-sentence, so only the opening diagnosis is available, not the promised regional-security proposal.

insights.claim: The memorandum of understanding that Tehran and Washington struck in Switzerland in June 2026 has fallen apart after hanging by a thread for weeks, and the United States has resumed attacks on Iran.
insights.speaker: Mohammad Javad Zarif
insights.so_what: A confirmed return to active U.S.-Iran hostilities removes the de-escalation premium from oil, tanker rates and regional risk assets.
insights.locator: The United States has resumed attacks on Iran

insights.claim: President Trump publicly wrote off diplomacy with Iran on July 8, 2026, saying 'I think it's over' and that he did not want to deal with Iran anymore.
insights.speaker: Mohammad Javad Zarif
insights.so_what: Explicit presidential abandonment of the track means the base case shifts to sustained military pressure rather than renewed negotiation — watch for Hormuz interdiction risk.
insights.quote: “I think it’s over,” U.S. President Donald Trump said on July 8. “I don’t want to deal with [Iran] anymore.”
insights.locator: The memorandum of understanding that Tehran and Washington struck

insights.claim: Iran's former foreign minister argues the memorandum's collapse was predictable rather than surprising, because Iran and the United States held divergent interpretations of the agreement's provisions from the outset.
insights.speaker: Mohammad Javad Zarif
insights.so_what: Signals from a senior Iranian insider that deliberately ambiguous deal text is structurally unstable — a template for discounting future headline U.S.-Iran agreements.
insights.quote: That the memorandum collapsed is not surprising.
insights.locator: That the memorandum collapsed is not surprising

insights.claim: The specific fault line that broke the deal was the Strait of Hormuz provisions, where Tehran believed it had only promised to 'make arrangements using its best efforts' rather than to guarantee an outcome.
insights.speaker: Mohammad Javad Zarif
insights.so_what: Hormuz transit is the contested clause, so the failure point maps directly onto the world's most important oil chokepoint — tanker insurance and crude spreads are the live expression.
